en: At the site of the prayer ritual, an altar is established for five days; at each altar, seven monks are provided with scattered food and lamps are lit.
Each night, the *Mahāpratisarā* [dhāraṇī] is chanted.

One roll of cloth. One camel hide. One sheet of paper. The above items are offered for the purpose of establishing an altar, reciting scriptures, making offerings to the monks, chanting the Buddha’s name, and lighting lamps.

May the Eight Divisions of Devas and Dragons provide protection; may the Four Heavenly Kings of Brahmā and Śakra guard Dunhuang; may the people be at peace and the borders tranquil. May all misfortunes depart for distant lands with the passing of the old year, and may every auspicious omen and favorable sign follow [the donor] within the Central Heavens of this Prefecture.
The Emperor and his sovereign protectors, following the great design, returned to the capital;
all within the eight quarters arrived to present their homage.
Your Majesty maintains your station, and your honors and blessings flourish daily.
Equaling the Five Peaks in height,
they match the heavens without fail;
the Princesses of Eternal Peace are as fragrant as peach and plum blossoms.

Furthermore, how could one take for granted that spring flowers would always flourish? [The inscription] records the extraordinary talent of [the subject], whose complete abilities were such that even among the young masters, he was uniquely filial and devoted to the state.
The young ladies and sisters dwell within their chambers, refining themselves with excellence;
the entire household is adorned with joy as they receive blessings.

Thereafter, the herding boys celebrate the prosperity of the Age of Shun, while the village elders sow the fields in celebration of the auspiciousness of Yao’s Golden Age, as the realm enjoys peace and security.
The five grains have doubled in every thousand households;
they overflow on the eastern mounds and are gathered in abundance across the southern fields.
May the imperial court send an envoy to early pay homage to the celestial countenance.
Regarding the frontier intelligence reported, it has indeed been granted by Your Majesty that the calamities have been swiftly extinguished.

May [the people] exert themselves so that the barbarian blades are hidden away and the smoke of war is forever ceased. Now, as the altar ceremony concludes, I approach the site of the field; may the Three Honored Ones, out of compassion, graciously dedicate these merits toward this end.
The twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month in the second year of the Changxing era: [the troops of] Xiguīyì and others.
